name: Ankle Circles
description: Gentle rotation of the ankles to improve circulation and flexibility before exercise.
steps: Sit comfortably in a chair with feet flat on the floor.
Lift one foot slightly off the floor.
Rotate the ankle slowly in a clockwise circle 10 times.
Reverse direction and rotate 10 times counter-clockwise.
Repeat with the other foot.
safetyTips: Keep movements slow and controlled.
Stop if you feel any pain or discomfort.

name: Shoulder Rolls
description: Rolling the shoulders forward and backward to release tension and warm up the upper body.
steps: Sit or stand with your back straight.
Slowly roll both shoulders forward in a circular motion 5 times.
Reverse and roll shoulders backward 5 times.
Keep your neck relaxed throughout.
safetyTips: Do not hunch your back.
Keep movements smooth and gentle.

name: Neck Side Stretch
description: Gentle lateral neck stretches to release tension and improve range of motion.
steps: Sit upright in a chair.
Slowly tilt your head to the right, bringing your ear toward your shoulder.
Hold for 10 seconds.
Return to center and repeat on the left side.
Perform 3 repetitions on each side.
safetyTips: Never force the stretch.
Stop if you feel dizziness or sharp pain.

name: Wrist Flexion and Extension
description: Bending and extending the wrists to warm up the joints and improve flexibility.
steps: Extend one arm in front of you with palm facing down.
Use the other hand to gently bend the wrist downward. Hold 10 seconds.
Then gently bend the wrist upward. Hold 10 seconds.
Repeat with the other wrist.
safetyTips: Apply gentle pressure only.
Avoid this exercise if you have wrist injuries.

name: Single Leg Stand
description: Standing on one leg to improve balance and strengthen stabilizing muscles.
steps: Stand behind a sturdy chair and hold the back for support.
Slowly lift one foot off the floor.
Hold the position for 10 seconds.
Lower the foot and repeat on the other side.
Perform 3 repetitions on each side.
safetyTips: Keep a chair or wall nearby for support.
Focus your gaze on a fixed point to help with balance.
Do not lock your standing knee.

name: Tandem Stand
description: Standing with one foot directly in front of the other to challenge balance.
steps: Stand near a wall or chair for support.
Place one foot directly in front of the other, heel touching toe.
Hold this position for 10 seconds.
Switch feet and repeat.
Perform 3 repetitions on each side.
safetyTips: Have support nearby at all times.
Look straight ahead, not down at your feet.

name: Weight Shifting
description: Shifting body weight from side to side to improve dynamic balance.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a chair for support.
Slowly shift your weight to the right foot.
Hold for 5 seconds, then shift to the left foot.
Repeat 10 times on each side.
safetyTips: Move slowly and deliberately.
Keep your core engaged.

name: Heel-to-Toe Walk
description: Walking in a straight line placing heel directly in front of toe to challenge balance.
steps: Stand at one end of a clear path.
Place your right heel directly in front of your left toe.
Continue walking heel-to-toe for 10 steps.
Turn around carefully and walk back.
Perform 3 lengths.
safetyTips: Walk near a wall for support if needed.
Look ahead, not at your feet.

name: Seated Leg Press
description: Pressing legs against resistance while seated to strengthen quadriceps and glutes.
steps: Sit upright in a sturdy chair.
Place a resistance band around both feet.
Slowly extend both legs forward against the resistance.
Hold for 2 seconds, then slowly return.
Repeat 10 times.
safetyTips: Keep your back straight throughout.
Do not lock your knees at full extension.

name: Chair Squats
description: Sitting down and standing up from a chair to strengthen leg muscles.
steps: Stand in front of a sturdy chair with feet shoulder-width apart.
Slowly lower yourself toward the chair as if sitting down.
Lightly touch the seat, then stand back up.
Keep your weight in your heels.
Repeat 10 times.
safetyTips: Use armrests for support if needed.
Keep your knees behind your toes.
Do not drop heavily into the chair.

name: Calf Raises
description: Rising up on the toes to strengthen calf muscles and improve ankle stability.
steps: Stand behind a chair, holding the back for support.
Slowly rise up onto your toes.
Hold for 2 seconds.
Slowly lower back down.
Repeat 15 times.
safetyTips: Rise and lower slowly for maximum benefit.
Keep your core engaged.

name: Step-Ups
description: Stepping up and down on a low step to strengthen legs and improve coordination.
steps: Stand in front of a low, stable step.
Step up with your right foot, then bring your left foot up.
Step down with your right foot, then your left.
Repeat 10 times leading with the right foot.
Then repeat 10 times leading with the left foot.
safetyTips: Hold a railing if available.
Ensure the step is stable and non-slip.
Place the whole foot on the step.

name: Marching in Place
description: Lifting knees alternately while standing to improve cardiovascular fitness.
steps: Stand behind a chair, holding the back for support.
Lift your right knee to hip height.
Lower it and lift your left knee.
Continue alternating for 2 minutes.
Maintain a steady, comfortable pace.
safetyTips: Do not lift knees higher than comfortable.
Breathe steadily throughout.

name: Seated Cycling
description: Pedaling motion with the legs while seated to improve cardiovascular endurance.
steps: Sit upright in a sturdy chair.
Lift both feet slightly off the floor.
Pedal your legs in a cycling motion.
Continue for 3 minutes at a comfortable pace.
Rest and repeat.
safetyTips: Keep your back supported against the chair.
Stop if you feel short of breath.

name: Side Steps
description: Stepping side to side to improve lateral movement and cardiovascular fitness.
steps: Stand with feet together.
Step to the right with your right foot, then bring your left foot to meet it.
Step to the left with your left foot, then bring your right foot to meet it.
Continue for 2 minutes.
Increase speed gradually as you feel comfortable.
safetyTips: Keep a chair nearby for support.
Wear non-slip footwear.

name: Brisk Walking Intervals
description: Alternating between normal and brisk walking pace to build cardiovascular endurance.
steps: Walk at a normal pace for 2 minutes.
Increase to a brisk pace for 1 minute.
Return to normal pace for 2 minutes.
Repeat the cycle 3 times.
Cool down with a slow walk for 2 minutes.
safetyTips: Wear supportive footwear.
Walk on a flat, even surface.
Stop if you feel chest pain or dizziness.

name: Tai Chi Wave Hands
description: A flowing Tai Chi movement involving gentle arm waves to improve coordination and relaxation.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.
Raise both arms to shoulder height, palms facing down.
Slowly wave arms to the right while shifting weight to the right foot.
Wave arms to the left while shifting weight to the left foot.
Continue flowing side to side for 2 minutes.
safetyTips: Move slowly and breathe deeply.
Keep knees soft, never locked.

name: Tai Chi Cloud Hands
description: A circular arm movement in Tai Chi that promotes upper body coordination and mindfulness.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Raise your right hand to eye level, palm facing you.
Move your right hand in a large circle to the right while your left hand moves in a circle to the left.
Shift your weight as your hands move.
Continue for 10 repetitions on each side.
safetyTips: Focus on smooth, continuous movement.
Breathe in through the nose, out through the mouth.

name: Tai Chi Grasp the Sparrow's Tail
description: A foundational Tai Chi sequence combining ward-off, roll-back, press, and push movements.
steps: Begin in a relaxed standing position.
Step forward with your right foot into a bow stance.
Perform the ward-off movement with your right arm.
Transition to roll-back, drawing both hands back.
Press forward with both palms.
Push forward with both palms.
Repeat on the left side.
safetyTips: Learn each movement slowly before combining them.
Keep your spine upright throughout.

name: Tai Chi Single Whip
description: A Tai Chi posture that stretches the arms wide and improves shoulder flexibility and balance.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend your right arm to the right with fingers pointing down (hook hand).
Extend your left arm to the left with palm facing forward.
Shift your weight to the left foot.
Hold for 5 seconds, then return to center.
Repeat on the other side.
safetyTips: Do not overextend your arms.
Keep your shoulders relaxed.

name: Indoor Walking Circuit
description: Walking a set circuit indoors to build endurance and practice safe walking patterns.
steps: Clear a safe walking path indoors (hallway or large room).
Walk at a comfortable pace from one end to the other.
Turn carefully at each end.
Complete 5 laps.
Rest for 1 minute, then complete 5 more laps.
safetyTips: Ensure the path is clear of obstacles.
Wear supportive, non-slip footwear.
Use a walking aid if needed.

name: Outdoor Walk — Flat Surface
description: A structured outdoor walk on a flat surface to build cardiovascular fitness and confidence.
steps: Choose a flat, even outdoor path.
Walk for 10 minutes at a comfortable pace.
Rest if needed, then continue.
Gradually increase duration by 2 minutes each week.
Return home safely.
safetyTips: Carry a mobile phone.
Inform someone of your route.
Wear a hat and sunscreen in hot weather.

name: Outdoor Walk — Incline
description: Walking on a gentle incline to increase exercise intensity and strengthen leg muscles.
steps: Find a gentle hill or inclined path.
Walk uphill for 5 minutes at a comfortable pace.
Turn around and walk downhill slowly.
Repeat 2 times.
Cool down with 5 minutes of flat walking.
safetyTips: Take shorter steps going uphill.
Lean slightly forward on inclines.
Use a walking stick for extra support.

name: Timed Up and Go Practice
description: Practicing the Timed Up and Go test to improve functional mobility.
steps: Sit in a chair with armrests.
On a signal, stand up from the chair.
Walk 3 meters to a marked point.
Turn around and walk back.
Sit back down in the chair.
Repeat 3 times, resting between attempts.
safetyTips: Have someone nearby to assist if needed.
Ensure the path is clear.
Use your walking aid if you normally use one.

name: Floor to Chair Recovery
description: Practicing the safe technique for getting up from the floor after a fall.
steps: Start lying on your back on a mat.
Roll onto your side.
Push yourself up to a hands-and-knees position.
Crawl to a sturdy chair.
Place both hands on the seat of the chair.
Bring one foot forward into a kneeling lunge position.
Push up to standing using the chair for support.
safetyTips: Practice on a soft mat.
Have someone nearby the first few times.
Take your time — there is no rush.

name: Controlled Lowering to Floor
description: Practicing how to lower yourself safely to the floor in a controlled manner.
steps: Stand next to a sturdy chair.
Hold the chair with both hands.
Slowly lower yourself to one knee.
Lower the other knee to the floor.
Gently lower yourself to a sitting position.
Then lie down slowly.
Reverse the steps to get back up.
safetyTips: Use a padded mat.
Never rush the movement.
Have a helper present initially.

name: Post-Fall Confidence Drill
description: A drill combining floor recovery with balance exercises to build confidence after a fall.
steps: Practice the floor-to-chair recovery technique.
Once standing, perform 5 single-leg stands.
Walk 5 meters and return.
Repeat the full sequence 2 times.
Focus on calm, controlled movements throughout.
safetyTips: Only attempt when feeling confident.
Have a carer or family member present.
Stop if you feel dizzy or unwell.

name: Seated Floor Sit Practice
description: Practicing sitting on the floor and getting up using a chair for support.
steps: Place a sturdy chair against a wall.
Hold the chair seat and slowly lower to the floor.
Sit comfortably on the floor for 30 seconds.
Roll to one side and get back to kneeling.
Use the chair to push up to standing.
safetyTips: Use a non-slip mat.
Ensure the chair is stable and against a wall.

name: Seated Forward Bend
description: A gentle seated stretch to cool down the hamstrings and lower back after exercise.
steps: Sit on the edge of a chair with legs extended.
Slowly lean forward from the hips.
Reach toward your feet as far as comfortable.
Hold for 20 seconds.
Slowly return to upright.
Repeat 3 times.
safetyTips: Do not bounce during the stretch.
Breathe out as you lean forward.

name: Standing Quad Stretch
description: Stretching the quadriceps while standing to reduce muscle tension after exercise.
steps: Stand behind a chair, holding the back for support.
Bend your right knee and bring your heel toward your buttock.
Hold your ankle with your right hand.
Hold for 20 seconds.
Lower the foot and repeat on the left side.
safetyTips: Keep your standing knee slightly bent.
Do not pull your ankle forcefully.

name: Deep Breathing Cool Down
description: Slow, deep breathing to lower heart rate and promote relaxation after exercise.
steps: Sit comfortably in a chair.
Place one hand on your chest and one on your abdomen.
Breathe in slowly through your nose for 4 counts.
Hold for 2 counts.
Breathe out slowly through your mouth for 6 counts.
Repeat 10 times.
safetyTips: Do not force your breath.
Stop if you feel lightheaded.

name: Seated Spinal Twist
description: A gentle seated rotation to stretch the spine and release tension after exercise.
steps: Sit upright in a chair with feet flat on the floor.
Place your right hand on your left knee.
Slowly rotate your torso to the left.
Hold for 15 seconds.
Return to center and repeat on the other side.
Perform 3 repetitions on each side.
safetyTips: Rotate only as far as comfortable.
Keep your hips facing forward.
